title: Entergy Mississippi invests in the future workforce through STEM scholarships for students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: The company’s Power of Prosperity program equips recipients with tools for success through education, career and workforce development programs
body_markdown:
JACKSON, Miss. – Entergy Mississippi is investing in the future of higher education and workforce development by awarding $20,000 in STEM scholarships to four outstanding students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities, or HBCUs, and partner institutions across Mississippi. The scholarships are part of Entergy’s $20 Million Power of Prosperity initiative, which supports HBCUs and minority-serving institutions across the Gulf South to help remove barriers to students’ academic success.


The initiative pillars include academic scholarships, workforce development including student internships, mentoring and faculty externships; generational wealth-building; and competitive facility grants and endowments. Scholarships are awarded to students pursuing degrees in high-demand fields such as computer science, information technology, engineering and related disciplines that align with the evolving energy workforce.


“These students represent the future of our communities across the Gulf South region. Their talent, determination and ambition will help shape the next generation of innovation, industry and economic development across our state,” said Haley Fisackerly, Entergy Mississippi president and CEO. “By investing in their education today, we’re not only opening doors of opportunity, we’re building a stronger, more resilient workforce that will support our communities for years to come.”


The Competitive Facilities Grant portion of the program will provide up to $1 million in funding this year for accredited HBCUs and Minority Serving Institutions in Entergy’s service area to help upgrade classrooms, labs, and equipment. Awards will be announced during the fall semester.


The 2026 scholarship recipients are:


**Hugo Estrada**


Jackson State University


Electrical and Computer Engineering


**Damian Ohajunwa**


Jackson State University


Computer and Information


**Ebuka Chibudem Uzoama**


Jackson State University


Computer and Information Sciences


**Antoine Washington**


Alcorn State University


Electromechanical Engineering


[Learn more here](https://www.entergy.com/news/entergy-makes-20m-commitment-empower-historically-black-colleges-universities-students) about Entergy’s Power of Prosperity program.


**About Entergy Mississippi**


Entergy Mississippi provides electricity to approximately 459,000 customers in 45 counties. Entergy Mississippi is a subsidiary of Entergy Corporation. Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for more than 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, we deliver more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees. Learn more at
